Every C# source file must begin with a correctly formatted copyright header.

What The Standard says

“Open Code” — The Standard treats source availability and stewardship as engineering concerns. A consistent ownership header makes the source's provenance explicit. read it here.
“Last Day” — The Standard requires work to be left in a state another engineer can pick up immediately. A uniform header is cCoder's mechanical addition to that continuity and provenance goal. read it here.

Why it matters

A consistent copyright header records ownership and licensing at the source-file boundary. Mechanical enforcement prevents newly generated or copied files from silently falling outside the project's declared legal convention.

Bad code example

// Violates STXFORMAT011: Every C# source file must begin with a correctly formatted copyright header.
namespace Students;

class Student { }

Good code example

// Follows STXFORMAT011
// ---------------------------------------------------------------
// Copyright (c) Paul.Ward@ccoder.co.uk
// ---------------------------------------------------------------

namespace Students;
